_arch_independent: Five entries (audiomass, cinny, drawio, element-call, minipaint) pin ONE artefact under the exclusive `any` key. Listing the same URL and digest under both amd64 and arm64 would look identical in the data to a curator pinning the amd64 asset under both — the kerf v0.1.9 shape — and scripts/verify-firstparty-artifacts.sh refuses two architectures sharing one sha256 for exactly that reason. The recipe states which it means instead of a checker guessing.
_ownership: NO RECIPE HERE CHOWNS ITS OWN STATE. Seven of these entries used to carry `chown -R 65534:65534 data` in post_install — a stopgap repeated seven times, silently absent from the eighth, and a PRIVILEGED command inside a string that also runs on a developer box, where it fails and POSTINSTALL-01 turns that failure into a failed install. InstallFromRegistry now hands the state directory to uid 65534 centrally, after post_install and through the data symlink (STATE-01, backend/services/appnet/state_owner.go). bin/ and static/ stay ROOT-owned on purpose: they are code, and an app that can rewrite its own binary keeps any compromise across a restart.
_measurement: EVERY checksum below was computed from bytes downloaded on 2026-08-17 and was written into this file BY A SCRIPT reading those measurements — no digest was typed by hand, because hand-copying twenty-two digests is exactly how a fabricated one enters a catalogue. Five of them (conduit amd64, gitea amd64, navidrome amd64, cinny, element-call, drawio) turned out to be byte-identical to digests the shipped registry already carried from an independent earlier measurement; those six agreements are the control on the run.
_not_verified: NO INSTALL WAS RUN. These recipes are pinned and their archive layouts were read out of the downloaded archives, but scripts/verify-app-recipe.sh has not been executed for any of them and roadmap/app-verification-ledger.json is untouched. `command`, `port` and `post_install` are therefore UNPROVEN. Every entry that ships _disabled today stays _disabled here.
_signing: UNSIGNED BY CONSTRUCTION — every entry carries "signature": "". VerifyEntrySignature fails closed on an empty signature, so these are inert until the founder's ceremony (`make sign-registry RELEASE_PRIV=…`). Do not set VULOS_SIGN_ALLOW_KEY_MISMATCH.
_source: registry.d/vulos-native.json — the apt/raw-shell/single-download entries re-expressed in the ONE Vulos-native install format (roadmap/INSTALL-METHODOLOGY.md). Staged for the single writer of registry.json; do NOT merge without re-signing.

audiomass._note: `git clone --depth=1` of the DEFAULT BRANCH -> a COMMIT-pinned source archive. AudioMass publishes no GitHub release at all (the releases API returns 404), so there is no tag to pin and the old recipe installed whatever master happened to be that day — the reproducibility failure this whole migration is about, in its purest form. Pinned to commit 2ac3801a476822c236d9914f9ef4d2d01f9131e6 (2026-05-25). The site lives in src/, so archive_strip is 2. The version key is the commit date because upstream declares no version. ARCH KEY: this uses artifacts.any rather than the same URL listed under amd64 and arm64. Those two encodings are indistinguishable from the data, and the second one IS the kerf v0.1.9 defect — three 'per-platform' tarballs that were one identical file. `any` is a claim that the payload carries no machine code, and it is exclusive so it can never act as a fallback.
audiomass.author: pkalogiros
audiomass.description: Browser-based audio editor — lightweight waveform editing, cut/copy/paste, effects, and format export; replaces Audacity for quick edits
audiomass.name: AudioMass

cinny._note: raw shell -> artifacts. The old recipe was wget + inline sha256sum + tar, which is the exact shape INSTALL-01 removes; the digest it checked is byte-identical to the one measured here. The payload is a static bundle and therefore architecture-independent, declared with the exclusive `any` artefact key. extract_dir keeps it out of the app root: `--directory .` would serve data/, which is a symlink to the owner's data directory. code-server._note: THE ENTRY THAT NAMED THIS PROBLEM. Its recipe carried a FABRICATED sha256 piped into `|| true`, so `dpkg -i` ran whatever the network returned. Now pinned to real per-arch digests measured today, and arm64 is gained (the old recipe was amd64 .deb only). IT STAYS _disabled DELIBERATELY: it was disabled for a TRUST failure, and re-enabling it on the strength of an install nobody has run would be the same mistake in the other direction. Enable it after `scripts/verify-app-recipe.sh code-server` passes, not before.

conduit._note: amd64 -> amd64+arm64. The shipped recipe named the binary `bin/conduwuit-linux-amd64` in `command`, so the arm64 asset that has been in the same release all along could never be used: one command string, one arch-specific filename. binary_name pins both to bin/conduwuit. The port is a LITERAL because ${PORT} is not expanded during post_install (only into `command`, at launch) and appPort is taken verbatim from this recipe's `port`. The amd64 digest is byte-identical to the one the shipped entry already carried, which is the control on this whole measurement run.

gitea._note: amd64-in-practice -> amd64+arm64. The shipped recipe was a shell string that curl'd the amd64 asset, checked a sha256 inline, and symlinked the binary into /usr/local/bin — a write outside the app dir that no boot path preserves. The digest it checked is byte-identical to the one measured here, so the recipe was honest; the SHAPE was the problem.

grafana._note: vendor-apt -> pinned upstream tarball, amd64+arm64. The tarball carries bin/, conf/ and public/ under one top-level directory, so archive_strip 1 unpacks it at the app root and --homepath . is the app dir the launcher sets as cwd. Replaces `wget -qO- apt.grafana.com/gpg.key | gpg --dearmor` — a key fetched over the network with no pin, which is what the old recipe's integrity rested on. dl.grafana.com publishes a .sha256 beside each asset; it was NOT cross-checked here, only the bytes were hashed.

grafana.description: Monitoring dashboards — visualize metrics from Prometheus, InfluxDB, PostgreSQL, and more
grafana.name: Grafana

minipaint._note: `git clone --depth=1 --branch v4.10.0` -> a checksum-pinned source archive. The clone pinned a TAG, which upstream can move; the digest cannot. CAVEAT, stated rather than buried: GitHub generates tag archives on demand, and a regenerated archive would change the digest. That fails CLOSED — a loud checksum mismatch — which is strictly better than a clone silently fetching different bytes. ARCH KEY: this uses artifacts.any rather than the same URL listed under amd64 and arm64. Those two encodings are indistinguishable from the data, and the second one IS the kerf v0.1.9 defect — three 'per-platform' tarballs that were one identical file. `any` is a claim that the payload carries no machine code, and it is exclusive so it can never act as a fallback.

navidrome._note: amd64-only -> amd64+arm64. The tarball has no top-level directory (LICENSE, README.md, navidrome at the root), so archive_strip is 0 and extract_dir puts them under bin/, which is what `command` names. Port literal: ${PORT} is not expanded in post_install and this entry relied on it. amd64 digest matches the one the shipped entry already carried.

syncthing._note: vendor-apt -> pinned upstream tarball, amd64+arm64. Replaces a recipe that added apt.syncthing.net with a GPG key fetched at install time and NOT pinned by sha256 — which APP-RECIPE-STANDARD §2.2 already says is vendor-download with extra steps. VERSION BUMP, and it is a real one: Debian/apt shipped the 1.x series and this pins 2.1.3, which changed the database format. Upstream's own sha256sum.txt.asc is published beside the assets and was NOT cross-checked here; only the bytes were hashed.
